Rashi on Chullin 91a:10:1.hebrew: ולר' יהודה איצטריך - דאע"ג דתרוייהו דאיסורא, קא פטר ליה בחד מלקות, וטעמא כדמפרש לקמיה, שאין בין שניהם אלא כזית. ואי מספקא ליה, אמאי לקי אפילו חדא? דילמא תרוייהו דהיתירא, הואיל ושתיהן ימניות:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:10:1.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda it was necessary - [That is,] even though both [sciatic nerves] are forbidden, he lets him off with [only] one [set of] lashes; and the reason is as [the Gemara] explains further on, that between the two of them there is only an olive's bulk. And if he were in doubt [as to which thigh is forbidden], why would he receive lashes even once? Perhaps both are permitted, since both are right [thighs]:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:11:1.hebrew: אכלו - גיד שלם, חייב; כאוכל נמלה כל שהוא, שהוא חייב משום דבריה הוא וחשיב איסור:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:11:1.english: He ate it - [Meaning, if he ate] an entire sinew, he is liable — like one who eats an ant of any size, who is liable because it is a complete entity [beryah] and is [therefore] considered a significant prohibition:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:12:1.english: What is the reason - [that] it is obvious to Rabbi Yehuda that [it is the one] of the right [thigh]?

Rashi on Chullin 91a:13:1.hebrew: ההוא - הא דכתיב "הירך", לאשמועינן אתא דבההוא גיד קאי:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:13:1.english: That one - That which is written, "the thigh," comes to teach us that [the verse] refers to that [specific] nerve:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:13:2.hebrew: דפשיט איסוריה בכוליה ירך - הוא וקנוקנותיו ושרשיו נפשטין בכל הירך, והיינו גיד הפנימי הגדול הנמצא בתחלת פריעת הירך:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:13:2.english: Whose prohibition spreads throughout the entire thigh - It, its tendrils, and its roots spread throughout the entire thigh; and this is the large inner sinew that is found at the beginning of uncovering the thigh:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:14:1.english: Who hugs another - from in front of him:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:14:2.english: And his hand - [his] right [hand] reaches the hollow of his fellow's right thigh from behind him:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:15:1.hebrew: כעובד כוכבים נדמה לו - כסבור היה יעקב שהוא עובד כוכבים, וטפלו לימינו כדי שיהא מזומן לאוחזו אם יקום עליו, ובירך הסמוכה לו נגע:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:15:1.english: He appeared to him as a gentile - Jacob thought that he was a gentile, and positioned him to his right so that he would be ready to seize him if he should rise up against him, and [thus he] touched the thigh nearest to him:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:15:2.english: He joins him to his right - He attaches him to the right.

Rashi on Chullin 91a:16:1.hebrew: כת"ח נדמה לו - וחלק לו יעקב כבוד כאילו הוא רבו, וטפלו לימינו כדי שיהא יעקב לשמאל המלאך:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:16:1.english: He appeared to him as a Torah scholar - And Jacob accorded him honor as though he were his teacher, and placed him at his right [side] so that Jacob would be to the left of the angel.

Rashi on Chullin 91a:16:2.hebrew: ה"ז בור - אין בו חכמת דרך ארץ:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:16:2.english: He is an ignoramus - he has no wisdom of proper conduct:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:17:1.hebrew: ורבנן - דפליגי אדרבי יהודה ואסרי בתרוייהו, קסברי: "מאחוריה אתא ונשייה בתרוייהו" — הכהו בשתיהם עד שנשו ממקומם ועלו:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:17:1.english: And the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi Yehudah and forbid [the sciatic nerve] in both [thighs], hold [that the angel] "came from behind him and displaced him in both" — he struck him in both of them until they slipped from their place and rose up:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:18:1.hebrew: האי בהאבקו מאי דרשת ביה - למה לי למכתביה כלל, אי לאו למימרא דכדרך הנאבקים נגע בו:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:18:1.english: What do you derive from this [phrase] "as he wrestled" - Why was it necessary [for Scripture] to write it at all, if not to say that he touched him in the manner of wrestlers:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:19:1.english: Left its place - It sprang [from its place]:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:19:2.english: Their might has left - their might sprang away [i.e., departed]:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:19:3.english: They have become as women - weak like women:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:1:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - מהכא לא תפשוט, וטעמא לאו משום ספיקא דגיד הוא, אלא מיפשט פשיטא ליה, והכא בשומן הגיד קאמר, דמותר מדאורייתא:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:1:1.english: Rav Ashi said - From here you cannot resolve [the question], and the reason is not because of a doubt regarding the sinew, rather it is obvious to him; and here he is speaking of the fat of the sinew, which is permitted by Torah law:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:1:2.hebrew: וישראל קדושים - העושין סייג לתורה, נהגו בו איסור, והלכך על כרחיך משייר ליה משום מנהגא, ושרפה בעי, הואיל ומדאורייתא בר אכילה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:1:2.english: And the Jewish people are holy - [Those] who make a fence around the Torah treated it as forbidden, and therefore, perforce, one leaves it over because of the custom, and it requires burning, since by Torah law it is fit to be eaten:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:20:1.english: The word that was sent to Jacob fell upon Israel - [meaning] upon all of Israel:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:21:1.hebrew: ופרע להן בית השחיטה - שלא יאמרו "בשר הנחירה אני אוכל", לפי שבני יעקב שומרי מצות היו, דאף על פי שלא נתנה תורה, מקובלין היו מאבותיהם:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:21:1.english: And expose the place of the slaughter to them - so that they would not say, "I am eating meat [from an animal killed by] stabbing," because the sons of Jacob were observers of the commandments, for even though the Torah had not [yet] been given, they had received [these traditions] from their forefathers:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:21:2.hebrew: כמאן דאמר - במתניתין (לקמן חולין דף ק:), גיד הנשה נאסר להם בעודם בני נח:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:21:2.english: According to the one who said - [as taught] in the Mishnah (later, Chullin 100b), [that] the sciatic nerve was forbidden to them while they were still descendants of Noah.

Rashi on Chullin 91a:22:1.hebrew: שנשתייר על פכים קטנים - דכל כלים החשובים ומקנה כבר העבירן את נחל יבק, כדכתיב לעיל מיניה: "ויעבר את כל אשר לו", והוא נשאר על פכין קטנים שלא הספיק להעביר, וחשכה לו:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:22:1.english: That he remained [behind] for small pitchers - For he had already brought all the important vessels and livestock across the Jabbok stream, as it is written just above it: "And he sent across all that he had" — and he remained [behind] for small pitchers that he had not managed to bring across, and it grew dark for him:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:23:1.hebrew: מדקאמר "עד עלות השחר", שמע מינה לא ניתנה רשות למזיק להזיק ביום, לפיכך לא הוצרך שמירה:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:23:1.english: Since [the verse] says "until the breaking of the day," learn from this [that] permission was not granted to a harmful spirit to cause harm during the day; therefore, [he] did not need protection [by day].

Rashi on Chullin 91a:23:2.english: From here [it is derived] that a Torah scholar, etc. - For Jacob remained alone and was injured:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:1.hebrew: פנימי הסמוך לעצם - הוא גיד ארוך, ונתון לארכו של שופי כשפורעין את הירך, ופושט בכל הירך: ראשו אחד מחובר בעצם האליה, ומשם נפשט לאורך השופי עד מקום חיבור הקולית ועצם הירך, ושם הוא סמוך לעצם:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:1.english: [The] inner [nerve] that is next to the bone - It is a long nerve, situated along the length of the fleshy slope of the thigh [shofi] when one strips open the thigh, and it extends throughout the entire thigh. One end of it is attached to the tailbone, and from there it extends along the fleshy slope of the thigh up to the junction of the femur [kolit] and the thighbone, and there it is next to the bone.

Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:3.hebrew: וחייבין עליו - מלקות, כדיליף לקמן מהירך; ועוד, שהוא על הכף, שהכף הוא בשר עגול הסובב את הקולית, דבוקה בה; ועל שם שהוא בצד פנימי של ירך — צד שכלפי ירך חברתה כשהבהמה מחוברת — קרי לה פנימי:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:3.english: And one is liable for it - [to receive] lashes, as [the Gemara] derives later from [the phrase] "the thigh" [in the verse]; and furthermore, because it is on the kaf [the hip-socket muscle], for the kaf is [the] round flesh that surrounds the femur [and] is attached to it; and because it is on the inner side of [the] thigh — [the] side that is toward the thigh of its counterpart when the animal is [whole and] joined together — [Shmuel] calls it "inner":

Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:4.hebrew: ואין חייבים עליו - דלאו היינו על הכף אלא בתוך הכף; ובההוא חיצון עסקינן, ומשייר ליה על כרחיה, ושרפה בעי, דהא מדאורייתא חזי:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:4.english: And one is not liable for it - for this [outer nerve] is not [located] upon the socket [of the thigh], but rather within the socket; and it is with that outer [nerve] that we are dealing [in the Mishnah], and he leaves it over perforce, and it requires burning [as leftover sacrificial meat], since by Torah law it is fit [to be eaten]:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:5.hebrew: וחיצון - גיד קצר הנתון לרוחב השופי בסופו, מובלע בכף הסובבת את הקולית, והוא נתון בצד חיצון של ירך:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:5.english: And the outer [nerve] - [This is] a short nerve that is situated across the width of the shofi [the tapering part of the thigh] at its end, embedded in the kaf [the hollow/socket-flesh] that surrounds the femur [kolit], and it is situated on the outer side of the thigh:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:2:6.english: [The outer nerve] is forbidden - by rabbinic law:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:3:1.hebrew: מזה כזית ומזה כזית - משל ימין ומשל שמאל. ומדנקט "אכל מזה כזית ומזה כזית", ולא נקט "אכל ב' זיתים משניהם", ש"מ שתי אכילות ושתי התראות הוו:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:3:1.english: From this an olive-bulk and from that an olive-bulk - [i.e.,] from the right [leg] and from the left [leg]. And since it states, "he ate an olive-bulk from this and an olive-bulk from that," and did not state, "he ate two olive-bulks from both of them," learn from this [that] there were two [separate] acts of eating and two warnings:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:4:1.english: Granted, if you say it is obvious to him - for this reason he incurs lashes for the right [sciatic nerve]:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:5:1.hebrew: הכה את זה - ספק בן ט' לזה, וספק בן ז' לזה:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:5:1.english: He struck this [one] - [referring to one who is] possibly a nine-[month] son of this [man], and possibly a seven-[month] son of that [man]:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:5:3.english: He is liable - for it is a certain forewarning:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:7:1.hebrew: בא הכתוב כו' - כבר פרשתי באותו ואת בנו, דכל מותיר התראת ספק היא; דכי מתרינן ביה "אל תותיר", מספקא לן אם עובר על התראה ואם לאו, דשמא קודם עלות השחר יאכלנו:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:7:1.english: The verse comes, etc. - I have already explained in [the chapter] Oto ve'et Beno that any [case of] leaving over [sacrificial meat] involves an uncertain warning; for when we warn him, "Do not leave [any] over," we are in doubt whether he is transgressing the warning or not, since perhaps before dawn he will eat it:

Rashi on Chullin 91a:9:1.hebrew: משתי בהמות - מדנקט "משתי בהמות", כי היכי דניהוי תרוייהו ימניות נקט; דאי ימין ושמאל, מה לי שתי בהמות ומה לי אחת:
Rashi on Chullin 91a:9:1.english: From two animals - Since [the baraita] stated "from two animals," it stated [this] so that both [thighs] would be right [thighs]; for if [it were speaking of] a right [thigh] and a left [thigh], what difference is there to me [whether they are from] two animals, and what difference is there to me [whether they are from] one [animal]?

Tosafot on Chullin 91a:1:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר לא נצרכא אלא לשמנו של גיד - לא קאי אדרב חסדא, דמוקי לה כר' יהודה; ולפי מה שאמר לקמן דלר' יהודה שמנו של גיד אפילו מדרבנן שרי, לא אתיא אלא כרבי מאיר. והא דלא קאמר רב אשי "אליבא דר"מ", משום דבברייתא דמייתי לא הוזכר בה ר"מ. וכן רבינא, דמוקי לה בגיד החיצון דהוי מדרבנן, לכאורה לא אתי כרבי יהודה; דלקמן מפיק לה מ"הירך" דפשיט ליה בכוליה ירך, לאפוקי חיצון דלא, ורבי יהודה דריש "הירך" — המיומנת שבירך; אם לא נאמר דתרתי שמעת מינה, דבלאו הכי דריש ליה לקמן (חולין דף צו:) לדרשה אחריתי, ונימא דכולהו מפיק מינה:
Tosafot on Chullin 91a:1:1.english: Rav Ashi said: [It] is necessary only for the fat of the sinew - [Rav Ashi] is not referring to Rav Ḥisda, who establishes [the Mishnah] in accordance with R' Yehuda; for according to what [the Gemara] says later, that according to R' Yehuda the fat of the sinew is permitted even by rabbinic law, [Rav Ashi's statement] accords only with R' Meir. And as for why Rav Ashi did not say "according to R' Meir," [it is] because in the baraita that he cites, R' Meir is not mentioned. And similarly, Ravina, who establishes [the Mishnah] as referring to the outer sinew, which is [prohibited] by rabbinic law, ostensibly does not accord with R' Yehuda; for later [the Gemara] derives [this] from "the thigh" — [meaning the sinew] that spreads throughout the entire thigh, to the exclusion of the outer [sinew], which does not — whereas R' Yehuda expounds "the thigh" [as meaning] the most prominent [part] of the thigh; unless we say that you learn two things from it — for in any case he expounds it later (Chullin 96b) for another exposition — and we say that he derives all of them from it:

Tosafot on Chullin 91a:21:1.hebrew: כמאן דאמר גיד הנשה נאסר לבני נח - וא"ת: דילמא לא נאסר, ואפילו הכי היו מקיימין, כמו שחיטה דקאמר ליה "פרע להם בית השחיטה"? וי"ל: מדקאמר "והכן", משמע דבלאו הכי לא משתרי. אי נמי, "פרע להו בית השחיטה" היינו נחירה, שנצטוו על הנחירה:
Tosafot on Chullin 91a:21:1.english: According to the one who said that the sciatic nerve was forbidden to the descendants of Noah - And if you say: Perhaps it was not forbidden, and even so they would observe [it], like ritual slaughter, where [Joseph] said to him, "Expose the place of the slaughter to them"? And one can say: From the fact that [Scripture] says, "and prepare," it implies that without this it is not permitted. Alternatively, "Expose the place of the slaughter to them" refers to stabbing, as they were commanded regarding stabbing:

Tosafot on Chullin 91a:23:1.hebrew: מכאן לתלמיד חכם שלא יצא יחידי בלילה - אומר ר"ת דדוקא נקט תלמיד חכם, משום דמזיקין מתקנאים בהם, כדאמרינן: ג' צריכין שימור: מלך, ות"ח, וחתן. והא דאמרן בריש פסחים (דף ב.): "לעולם יכנס אדם בכי טוב" כו', דמשמע כל אדם, מדלא נקט תלמיד חכם — התם מיירי ברחוק מן העיר, מפני המכשולות והליסטים:
Tosafot on Chullin 91a:23:1.english: From here [it is derived] that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night - Rabbeinu Tam says that [the Gemara] specifically mentioned a Torah scholar because harmful spirits are envious of them, as we say: Three require guarding: a king, a Torah scholar, and a groom. And as for that which we say at the beginning of Pesachim (2a): "A person should always enter [the city] while it is still light," etc., which implies any person, since it did not mention a Torah scholar — there it is speaking of [one who is] far from the city, because of obstacles and bandits:

Tosafot on Chullin 91a:4:1.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת ספוקי מספקא ליה כו' - ולא בעי לאוקומי שאכל שניהם בבת אחת, דהשתא לא הויא התראת ספק, כי היכי דלא נפשוט בעיא דאכל שני זיתי חלב בהעלם אחד דס"פ אותו ואת בנו (לעיל חולין דף פב:):
Tosafot on Chullin 91a:4:1.english: But if you say he is uncertain, etc. - And [the Gemara] did not want to establish [the case as one] where he ate both of them at once — for then it would not be an uncertain forewarning — so that we would not resolve the dilemma regarding one who ate two olive-bulks of forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness, [discussed] at the end of the chapter [entitled] Oto veEt Beno (above, Chullin 82b):
